plan.title: Direct Single-Stage RFQ Split Award to PO

steps.note: Open the direct single-stage event creation flow without a purchase request.
Set the event type to RFQ and enable line-item allocation for a split award.
Provide the mandatory event title.
Apply the first available RFQ template so the pricing sheet can be configured.
Add the requested CYLINDER line item with quantity 10.

args.goal: on the single-stage RFQ create screen, select CYLINDER WITH KEY & KNOB so Product Variant shows Default Variant, set Delivery location to Plant Name (LOC-0001), and stop on the completed pricing sheet

steps.note: Complete the product variant and delivery-location selections that no dedicated catalog step exposes.
Complete the remaining pricing-sheet fields.
Commit a 30-minute schedule starting now.
Invite two QA vendors for the two competing bids.
Publish the configured RFQ.
Verify that publication reached a real project page.
Submit Vendor 1's quote at 100.
Verify the first vendor's bid was accepted.
Submit Vendor 2's quote at 90.
Verify the second vendor's bid was accepted.
Close the bidding round so awarding is available.
Open the buyer's comparison grid after both bids are present.
Verify that both bidding vendors appear as real vendor columns.
Verify the first vendor's quoted rate.
Verify the second vendor's quoted rate.
Verify the comparison-grid amount arithmetic.
Open the awarding flow for the closed event.

args.goal: on the awarding screen, allocate 6 units to Vendor B and 4 units to Vendor A, create and submit the split award proposal, and stop on the submitted proposal page

steps.note: Perform the quantity split and proposal submission, which no catalog domain step can express directly.

args.need: sign in as the assigned approver and approve the submitted award proposal

steps.note: The case requires a separate approver account that the catalog cannot authenticate.
Create the purchase orders after the award has been approved.
Verify that the created purchase orders contain two awarded PO lines in total.
Return to the events list to verify the completed event's history placement.
Open the History tab.
Verify that this plan's event appears in History.
Reopen the plan's completed event to inspect its available actions.
Verify that Recreate Order remains available for the direct event.
